header.name: Alarm
header.description: Represents an alarm event generated from telemetry, including trigger details, timestamps, and workflow state.

modelDefinition.name: Alarm

fields.name: id
fields.description:
**`id`** (`ID!`)
Primary unique identifier for the Alarm record.

- Required on creation; cannot be updated.

fields.name: code
fields.description:
**`code`** (`String!`)
Unique, human-readable code for the Alarm.

- Used as the label field for UI and integrations.
- Example: `ALM-001`.

fields.name: deviation
fields.description:
**`deviation`** (`Float`)
Difference between the trigger value and the nominal/setpoint value at the time of alarm.

fields.name: limitValue
fields.description:
**`limitValue`** (`Float!`)
The configured threshold that was crossed to trigger the alarm.

fields.name: triggerValue
fields.description:
**`triggerValue`** (`Float!`)
The actual measured value that caused the alarm.

fields.name: limitType
fields.description:
**`limitType`** (`String!`)
Type of limit evaluation that triggered the alarm (e.g., `High`, `Low`, `Deviation`).

fields.name: notes
fields.description:
**`notes`** (`String`)
Free-form text for operator comments or corrective actions.

fields.name: acknowledgedAt
fields.description:
**`notes`** (`String`)
Free-form text for operator comments or corrective actions.

fields.name: clearedAt
fields.description:
**`clearedAt`** (`DateTime`)
Timestamp when the alarm condition returned to normal.

fields.name: triggeredAt
fields.description:
**`triggeredAt`** (`DateTime!`)
Timestamp when the alarm was first detected.

fields.name: duration
fields.description:
**`duration`** (`Duration`)
Total time the alarm was active (from triggered to cleared).

fields.name: alarmStateId
fields.description:
**`alarmStateId`** (`ID!`)
Foreign key referencing the current alarm state.

fields.name: alarmState
fields.description:
**`alarmState`** (`AlarmState!`)
Related AlarmState object for workflow state.

fields.name: acknowledgedByUserId
fields.description:
**`acknowledgedByUserId`** (`ID`)
Foreign key referencing the user who acknowledged the alarm.

fields.name: acknowledgedByUser
fields.description:
**`acknowledgedByUser`** (`User`)
Related User object for acknowledgment tracking.

fields.name: dataPointId
fields.description:
**`dataPointId`** (`ID`)
Foreign key linking the alarm to the originating DataPoint.

fields.name: dataPoint
fields.description:
**`dataPoint`** (`DataPoint`)
Related DataPoint object for telemetry context.

modelDefinition.description: Represents an alarm event generated from telemetry, including trigger details, timestamps, and workflow state.

header.name: AlarmState
header.description:
Represents a predefined state or condition for alarms in the system. Alarm states define how alarms are categorized, displayed, and prioritized for operational and safety workflows.

**Typical Use Cases**

- Define standard alarm states for machine telemetry (e.g., Active, Acknowledged, Cleared).
- Control alarm visibility and usability in dashboards.
- Apply sort order for consistent UI presentation.

modelDefinition.name: AlarmState

fields.name: id
fields.description:
The immutable, primary unique identifier for the AlarmState record.

- This means the `id` value is set equal to the `code` value during creation.**Behavior:** Automatically derived from the `code` field using the function:`$ ~> | $ | { "id": code }`

- **Usage:** Used for queries, filters, and as a unique key in related models.
- **Example:** If `code = "ACTIVE"`, then `id = "ACTIVE"`.

fields.name: code
fields.description:
**`code`** (`String!`)
A unique, human-readable code for the AlarmState.

- **Behavior:** Required at creation; can be updated.
- **Usage:** Serves as the label field for UI and integrations.
- **Example:** `ACTIVE`, `ACKNOWLEDGED`, `CLEARED`.
- **Constraint:** Must be unique within the tenant.

fields.name: sortOrder
fields.description:
**`sortOrder`** (`Int!`)
Numeric value that determines the display order of AlarmStates in lists or UI components.

- **Default:** `1`.
- **Usage:** Lower values appear first in sorted lists.
- **Example:** `1` for Active, `2` for Acknowledged.

fields.name: usable
fields.description:
**`usable`** (`Boolean!`)
Indicates whether the AlarmState is available for use in the system.

- **Default:** `true`.
- **Behavior:** When `false`, the state is hidden or disabled in workflows.
- **Example:** `true` (usable), `false` (disabled).

fields.name: name
fields.description:
**`name`** (`String!`)
Descriptive name of the AlarmState for display and reporting purposes.

- **Example:** `Active`, `Acknowledged`, `Cleared`.

fields.name: alarms
fields.description:
**`alarms`** (`[Alarm!]!`)
Collection of alarms associated with this AlarmState.

- **Behavior:**Relation enforced via `AlarmState.id → Alarm.alarmStateId`.
Included in queries and mutations for nested operations.
- **Usage:** Enables grouping alarms by state for dashboards and workflows.
- **Example:** `[ { id: "...", code: "ALM-001", description: "High Temperature" }, ... ]`.

header.name: Area
header.description:
Represents a functional or physical subdivision within a Site, such as an assembly zone, machining bay, or packaging section. Areas organize Lines and Cells into logical groups for scheduling, reporting, and operational control.

**Typical Use Cases**

- Group production lines for shift planning and maintenance campaigns.
- Apply area-level rules (e.g., safety procedures, blackout windows).
- Aggregate metrics for dashboards and compliance reporting.

modelDefinition.name: Area

fields.name: id
fields.description:
The immutable, primary unique identifier for the Area record.

- **Behavior:** Required on creation; cannot be updated.
- **Usage:** Used for queries, filters, and as a foreign key in related models (e.g., Lines reference Area via `areaId`).
- **Example:** `"a1b2c3d4-5678-90ef-ghij-1234567890ab"`

fields.name: code
fields.description:
A unique, human-readable code for the Area within its parent Site.

- **Behavior:** Required at creation; can be updated.
- **Usage:** Acts as the label field for UI and integrations.
- **Example:** `A01`, `ASSEMBLY-01`
- **Constraint:** Must be unique within the Site.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
The descriptive name of the Area for display and reporting purposes.

- **Example:** `Assembly Zone`, `Machining Bay`.

fields.name: isActive
fields.description:
Indicates whether the Area is active for scheduling, telemetry, and reporting.

- **Default:** `true`
- **Behavior:**When `false`, new operations should be blocked; historical data remains accessible.

- **Example:** `true` (operational), `false` (inactive).

fields.name: siteId
fields.description:
Foreign key linking the Area to its parent Site.

- **Behavior:** Required; ensures hierarchical integrity.
- **Usage:** Used in queries and mutations to associate the Area with a Site.
- **Example:** `"c3f1b3c0-8b3d-4b2b-9e3d-2f9e5b6a12cd"`

fields.name: site
fields.description:
The related Site object for this Area.

- **Behavior:**Relation enforced via `siteId → Site.id`.
Deletion of the Site is prevented if Areas exist.

- **Usage:** Enables nested queries and mutations for hierarchical data.
- **Example:** `{ id: "...", code: "DET-PLANT01", name: "Detroit Plant 1" }`

fields.name: lines
fields.description:
Collection of Lines associated with this Area.

- **Behavior:**Relation enforced via `Area.id → Line.areaId`.
Included in queries and mutations for nested operations.

- **Usage:** Represents the next level in the manufacturing hierarchy under the Area.
- **Example:** `[ { id: "...", code: "L01", name: "Assembly Line 1" }, ... ]`

header.name: Asset
header.description:
Represents a physical or logical piece of equipment, machine, or device within the manufacturing hierarchy. Assets are linked to Lines and Cells and include telemetry, maintenance schedules, and operational metadata. The model now supports linking to a **DeviceDriver** for integration and communication configuration.

**Typical Use Cases**

- Track machine details (manufacturer, model, serial number).
- Associate assets with Lines and Cells for production visibility.
- Manage preventive maintenance schedules (PM dates).
- Capture telemetry and data points for performance monitoring.
- Link to DeviceDriver for IoT and protocol-specific connectivity.

modelDefinition.name: Asset

fields.name: id
fields.description:
**`id`** (`ID!`)
The immutable, primary unique identifier for the Asset record.

- **Behavior:** Required on creation; cannot be updated.
- **Usage:** Used for queries, filters, and as a foreign key in related models.

fields.name: code
fields.description:
**`code`** (`String!`)
A unique, human-readable code for the Asset.

- **Behavior:** Required at creation; can be updated.
- **Usage:** Serves as the label field for UI and integrations.
- Uses a sequence value: "ASSET-" with a number and 0 padding of 3

fields.name: connectionString
fields.description:
**`connectionString`** (`String`)
Connection details for integrating the Asset with IoT or MES systems.

- **Example:** `opc.tcp://192.168.1.10:4840`.

fields.name: criticality
fields.description:
**`criticality`** (`String`)
Indicates the importance or risk level of the Asset.

- **Example:** `High`, `Medium`, `Low`.

fields.name: manufacturer
fields.description:
**`manufacturer`** (`String`)
The manufacturer of the Asset.

- **Example:** `ABB`, `Fanuc`.

fields.name: model
fields.description:
**`model`** (`String`)
The model identifier provided by the manufacturer.

- **Example:** `IRB 6700`.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
**`name`** (`String`)
Descriptive name of the Asset for display and reporting purposes.

- **Example:** `Welding Robot`, `Conveyor Belt`.

fields.name: responsibleTeam
fields.description:
**`responsibleTeam`** (`String`)
The team responsible for maintaining or operating the Asset.

- **Example:** `Maintenance`, `Production`.

fields.name: serialNumber
fields.description:
**`serialNumber`** (`String`)
Unique serial number assigned by the manufacturer.

- **Example:** `SN123456789`.

fields.name: status
fields.description:
**`status`** (`String`)
Current operational status of the Asset.

- **Example:** `Active`, `Inactive`, `Under Maintenance`.

fields.name: subType
fields.description:
**`subType`** (`String`)
More specific classification within the type.

- **Example:** `Welding`, `Inspection`.

fields.name: type
fields.description:
**`type`** (`String`)
High-level classification of the Asset.

- **Example:** `Machine`, `Robot`, `Sensor`.

fields.name: installedAt
fields.description:
**`installedAt`** (`Date`)
Date when the Asset was installed.

- **Example:** `2024-05-10`.

fields.name: lastPmAt
fields.description:
**`lastPmAt`** (`Date`)
Date of the last preventive maintenance performed.

- **Example:** `2025-12-15`.

fields.name: nextPmAt
fields.description:
**`nextPmAt`** (`Date`)
Scheduled date for the next preventive maintenance.

- **Example:** `2026-03-01`.

fields.name: deviceDriverId
fields.description:
**`deviceDriver`** (`DeviceDriver!`)
Link to the DeviceDriver configuration for this Asset.

- **Purpose:** Defines protocol, communication settings, and driver logic for IoT integration.
- **Example:** `{ id: "...", name: "OPC UA Driver", version: "1.2.0" }`.

fields.name: deviceDriver
fields.description:
**`dataPoints`** (`[DataPoint!]!`)
Collection of telemetry data points associated with the Asset.

- **Usage:** For IoT and real-time monitoring.
- **Example:** `[ { id: "...", tag: "Temperature", value: 75 }, ... ]`.

fields.name: dataPoints
fields.description:
**`dataPoints`** (`[DataPoint!]!`)
Collection of telemetry data points associated with the Asset.

- **Usage:** For IoT and real-time monitoring.
- **Example:** `[ { id: "...", tag: "Temperature", value: 75 }, ... ]`.

header.name: Cell
header.description:
Represents the smallest operational unit in the manufacturing hierarchy, such as a work cell, station, machine, or robotic unit. Cells capture real-time operational states, production counts, and quality metrics at the most granular level.

**Typical Use Cases**

- Monitor machine or station status (Run, Idle, Down, Setup).
- Collect production counts and reject rates for OEE calculations.
- Associate sensors, tags, and telemetry data for real-time visibility.
- Link to jobs and operators for execution tracking.

modelDefinition.name: Cell

fields.name: id
fields.description:
**`id`** (`ID!`)
The immutable, primary unique identifier for the Cell record.

- **Behavior:** Required on creation; cannot be updated.
- **Usage:** Used for queries, filters, and as a foreign key in related models.
- **Example:** `"c1d2e3f4-5678-90gh-ijkl-345678901234"`

fields.name: isActive
fields.description:
**`isActive`** (`Boolean!`)
Indicates whether the Cell is active for scheduling, telemetry, and reporting.

- **Default:** `true`.
- **Behavior:** When `false`, new operations should be blocked; historical data remains accessible.
- **Example:** `true` (operational), `false` (inactive).

fields.name: code
fields.description:
**`code`** (`String!`)
A unique, human-readable code for the Cell within its parent Line.

- **Behavior:** Required at creation; can be updated.
- **Usage:** Serves as the label field for UI and integrations.
- **Example:** `C01`, `STATION-01`.
- **Constraint:** Must be unique within the Line.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
**`name`** (`String`)
Descriptive name of the Cell for display and reporting purposes.

- **Example:** `Welding Station 1`, `Inspection Cell A`.

fields.name: lineId
fields.description:

fields.name: line
fields.description:

- **Behavior:**Relation enforced via `lineId → Line.id`.
Deletion of the Line is prevented if Cells exist.

- **Usage:** Enables nested queries and mutations for hierarchical data.
- **Example:** `{ id: "...", code: "L01", name: "Assembly Line 1" }`

header.name: DataPoint
header.description:
Represents a single telemetry or process variable associated with an Asset. DataPoints define how values are collected, scaled, validated, and monitored for alarms and historical tracking.

**Typical Use Cases**

- Capture real-time sensor readings or machine parameters.
- Apply scaling, limits, and deadband for accurate data acquisition.
- Enable alarms and warnings for critical thresholds.
- Historize data for trend analysis and reporting.
- Associate DataPoints with Assets and Units for contextual meaning.

modelDefinition.name: DataPoint

fields.name: id
fields.description:
**`id`** (`ID!`)
The immutable, primary unique identifier for the DataPoint record.

- **Behavior:** Required on creation; cannot be updated.
- **Usage:** Used for queries, filters, and as a foreign key in related models.

fields.name: code
fields.description:
**`code`** (`String!`)
Unique identifier for the DataPoint within its Asset.

fields.name: frequency
fields.description:
**`frequency`** (`Int!`)
Sampling frequency in milliseconds for periodic data collection.

- **Default:** `5000` (5 seconds).
- **Usage:** Determines how often the value is read when `isOnChange = false`.

fields.name: precision
fields.description:
**`precision`** (`Int!`)
Number of decimal places for the recorded value.

- **Default:** `2`.
- **Usage:** Controls rounding for display and storage.

fields.name: deadband
fields.description:
**`deadband`** (`Float!`)
Minimum change required to record a new value (for OnChange mode).

- **Default:** `0.0`.
- **Usage:** Reduces noise by ignoring insignificant changes.

fields.name: lowerLimit
fields.description:
**`lowerLimit`** (`Float`)
Minimum acceptable value for the DataPoint.

- **Default:** `0`.
- **Usage:** Used for validation and alarms.

fields.name: lowerWarning
fields.description:
**`lowerWarning`** (`Float`)
Warning threshold below normal operating range.

- **Default:** `0`.

fields.name: scaleFactor
fields.description:
**`scaleFactor`** (`Float!`)
Factor applied to raw values for scaling.

- **Default:** `1.0`.

fields.name: setPoint
fields.description:
**`setPoint`** (`Float`)
Target value for control or monitoring purposes.

fields.name: tolerance
fields.description:
**`tolerance`** (`Float!`)
Acceptable deviation from the setPoint.

- **Default:** `0.0`.

fields.name: upperLimit
fields.description:
**`upperLimit`** (`Float`)
Maximum acceptable value for the DataPoint.

- **Usage:** Used for validation and alarms.

fields.name: upperWarning
fields.description:
**`upperWarning`** (`Float`)
Warning threshold above normal operating range.

fields.name: alarmEnabled
fields.description:
**`alarmEnabled`** (`Boolean!`)
Indicates if alarms are active for this DataPoint.

- **Default:** `false`.

fields.name: enabled
fields.description:
**`enabled`** (`Boolean!`)
Indicates if the DataPoint is active for collection.

- **Default:** `true`.

fields.name: historize
fields.description:
**`historize`** (`Boolean!`)
Indicates if values should be stored historically.

- **Default:** `true`.

fields.name: isCritical
fields.description:
**`isCritical`** (`Boolean!`)
Marks the DataPoint as critical for operations.

- **Default:** `false`.

fields.name: isOnChange
fields.description:
**`isOnChange`** (`Boolean!`)
Determines collection mode:

- `true` = OnChange (record only when value changes beyond deadband).
- `false` = Periodic (based on frequency).
- **Default:** `false`.

fields.name: alarmPriority
fields.description:
**`alarmPriority`** (`String!`)
Priority level for alarms.

- **Default:** `Warning`.
- **Example:** `Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`.

fields.name: category
fields.description:
**`category`** (`String!`)
Logical grouping for the DataPoint.

- **Default:** `General`.

fields.name: dataType
fields.description:
**`dataType`** (`String!`)
Data type of the value.

- **Default:** `float`.
- **Example:** `int`, `boolean`, `string`.

fields.name: description
fields.description:
**`description`** (`String`)
Detailed description of the DataPoint.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description:
**`displayName`** (`String`)
Friendly name for UI display.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
**`name`** (`String`)
Internal name for the DataPoint.

fields.name: assetId
fields.description:
**`assetId`** (`ID!`)
Foreign key linking the DataPoint to its parent Asset.

fields.name: asset
fields.description:
**`asset`** (`Asset!`)
The related Asset object.

- **Behavior:** Relation enforced via `assetId → Asset.id`.
- **Deletion:** Cascade behavior (DataPoints removed if Asset is deleted).

fields.name: unitId
fields.description:
**`unitId`** (`ID!`)
Foreign key linking the DataPoint to a Unit of measure.

fields.name: unit
fields.description:
**`unit`** (`Unit!`)
The related Unit object.

- **Behavior:** Relation enforced via `unitId → Unit.id`.
- **Deletion:** Prevent behavior (cannot delete Unit if DataPoints exist).

fields.name: alarms
fields.description:
**`alarms`** (`[Alarm!]!`) Collection of alarms associated with this DataPoint.

- **Behavior:**Relation enforced via `DataPoint.id → Alarm.dataPointId`. Included in queries and mutations for nested operations.
- **Usage:** Enables grouping alarms by state for dashboards and workflows.
- **Example:** `[ { id: "...", code: "ALM-001", description: "High Temperature" }, ... ]`.

fields.name: telemetryRaws
fields.description:
**`telemetryRaws`** (`[TelemetryRaw!]!`)

Collection of raw telemetry records associated with this DataPoint.

- **Behavior:**Relation enforced via `DataPoint.id → TelemetryRaw.dataPointId`.
Included in queries and mutations for nested operations.

- **Usage:**Stores unprocessed or raw sensor values before scaling, filtering, or historization.
Useful for diagnostics, troubleshooting, and validating processed data against original readings.

fields.name: telemetryHourlies
fields.description:
**`telemetryHourlies`** (`[TelemetryHourly!]!`)

Collection of hourly aggregated telemetry records associated with this DataPoint.

- **Behavior:**Relation enforced via `DataPoint.id → TelemetryHourly.dataPointId`.
Included in queries and mutations for nested operations.

- **Usage:**Stores summarized telemetry data at an hourly interval for trend analysis, reporting, and performance dashboards.
Useful for reducing storage overhead compared to raw telemetry while retaining time-series insights.

fields.name: telemetryDailies
fields.description:
**`telemetryDailies`** (`[TelemetryDaily!]!`)

Collection of daily aggregated telemetry records associated with this DataPoint.

- **Behavior:**Relation enforced via `DataPoint.id → TelemetryDaily.dataPointId`.
Included in queries and mutations for nested operations.

- **Usage:**Stores summarized telemetry data at a daily interval for trend analysis, reporting, and KPI dashboards.
Useful for reducing storage overhead compared to raw telemetry while retaining essential insights for long-term analytics.

- Aggregate performance metrics from Cells for line-level KPIs.
- Apply shift profiles and capacity constraints for scheduling.
- Monitor real-time states and events for production optimization.
- Associate assets (machines, tools) for maintenance and telemetry.

header.name: Site
header.description:
Represents a physical location/campus (plant, distribution center, HQ) where operations, assets, and personnel are logically grouped. Top-level scope for facilities, compliance settings, and region-specific configurations.

**Typical Use Cases**

- Segregate production metrics, inventory, labor, and compliance by location.
- Scope access controls, schedules, and integrations to a physical site.

modelDefinition.name: Site

fields.name: id
fields.description:
**`id`** (`ID!`, unique, queryable, where-enabled, create-included, update-excluded)
 **What it is:** The immutable, primary unique identifier for a Site record.
 **Behavior:**

- Returned in queries and usable in `where` filters.
- Included on create; not updatable once persisted.
 **Examples:** `"c3f1b3c0-8b3d-4b2b-9e3d-2f9e5b6a12cd"`
 **Notes:** Every model must include an `id`. This key is used in relations (e.g., Areas reference Site via `siteId`).

fields.name: code
fields.description:
**`code`** (`String!`, unique, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** The human-friendly, unique label for the site, used as the main display (`labelField`) and common key in integrations.
 **Behavior:**

- Must be unique per tenant.
- Required at creation; can be updated (ensure downstream references are resilient).
 **Examples:** `DET-PLANT01`, `MX-GDL-DC1`
 **Recommended Pattern:** `[COUNTRY/REGION]-[CITY]-[FACILITY]` (e.g., `US-DET-PLT1`).

fields.name: isActive
fields.description:
**`isActive`** (`Boolean!`, default `true`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** Operational flag indicating whether the site is active for scheduling, telemetry, and reporting.
 **Behavior:**

- Defaults to `true` on creation.
- When `false`, new scheduling/jobs should be blocked; historical data remains accessible.
 **Examples:** `true` (operational), `false` (paused/archived).

fields.name: city
fields.description:
**`city`** (`String`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** City or municipality.
 **Examples:** `Detroit`.

fields.name: country
fields.description:
**`country`** (`String`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** Country name or code.
 **Examples:** `USA`, `US`, `Mexico`, `MX`.
 **Recommendation:** Normalize to ISO-3166 alpha-2 (e.g., `US`, `MX`) and keep a display mapping.

fields.name: industry
fields.description:
**`industry`** (`String`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** Industry classification for the site’s operations.
 **Examples:** `Automotive`, `Food & Beverage`, `Aerospace`, `Pharma`.
 **Usage:** Useful for reporting, filtering, and applying templates/policies.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
**`name`** (`String`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** The formal or long name of the site.
 **Usage:** For display purposes, documentation, and reporting.
 **Examples:** `Detroit Plant 1`, `Guadalajara Distribution Center`.

fields.name: postalCode
fields.description:
**`postalCode`** (`String`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** Postal or ZIP code.
 **Examples:** `48201`, `44940`.
 **Validation:** Optional format checks per country.

fields.name: state
fields.description:
**`state`** (`String`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** State/province/region (use ISO whenever possible).
 **Examples:** `MI`, `Jalisco`.
 **Note:** Consider normalizing to ISO-3166-2 codes in validation logic.

fields.name: street
fields.description:
**`street`** (`String`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** Street address line for logistics and compliance.
 **Examples:** `1234 Industrial Way`.

fields.name: timezone
fields.description:
**`timezone`** (`String`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** IANA timezone identifier used for job windows, OEE, and event timestamps.
 **Examples:** `America/Detroit`, `America/Mexico_City`.
 **Validation:** Ensure valid IANA TZ (e.g., via library or known list); this drives scheduling behavior.

*Note - you might use the tenant timezone setting instead - if ONLY supporting single site within the app.

fields.name: type
fields.description:
**`type`** (`String`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** Classification of the site.
 **Common Values:** `Plant`, `DistributionCenter`, `Headquarters`, `R&D`, `VendorManaged`.
 **Notes:** Use consistent enumerations in your app logic even though stored as string.

fields.name: areas
fields.description:
**`areas`** (`[Area!]!`, relation via `Site.id → Area.siteId`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** Collection of Areas associated to the Site.
 **Behavior:**

- Populated through relation: `from: "id"` (Site) to `to: "siteId"` (Area).
- Included in create/update inputs to allow nested operations if your mutation handlers support it.
 **Notes:** Typical hierarchy is **Site → Area → Line → Cell**; enforce referential integrity in mutations.

modelDefinition.description:

header.name: TelemetryRaw

Represents a raw telemetry record captured from a device or sensor before any processing, scaling, or historization. These records provide the original data values for diagnostics, validation, and troubleshooting.

**Typical Use Cases**

- Store unprocessed sensor readings for audit and verification.
- Support advanced analytics by comparing raw and processed values.
- Enable short-term retention for high-frequency data streams.

- **Example:** `"2026-01-04T09:20:00Z"`.

fields.name: dataPointId
fields.description:

fields.name: dataPoint

- **Behavior:**Relation enforced via `dataPointId → DataPoint.id`.

header.name: WorkcenterHistoryScheduler
header.description:
ISO 22400-Compliant Workcenter State Change Generator

This node generates realistic workcenter state changes for manufacturing simulation, strictly adhering to ISO 22400-2 standards for OEE calculation.

Core Functions:

- Processes workcenters in batches to simulate operational state transitions

- Maintains open history records (one active state per workcenter)

- Closes previous states and creates new states atomically

- Applies weighted randomness for realistic production patterns

- Enforces ISO 22400-compliant mode-state relationships

ISO 22400-2 Compliance:

The mode-state transition logic ensures proper OEE classification:

- PRODUCTION mode: Only states where equipment actively produces (running, running-slow)

- DISABLED mode: Unscheduled downtime states (faulted, blocked, starved, e-stopped)

- SETUP mode: Planned minor stops within production time (changeover, warmup, cleaning)

- IDLE mode: Planned idle time within production schedule (stopped)

- MAINTENANCE mode: Scheduled maintenance outside production (maintenance, offline)

- CLEANING mode: Deep cleaning activities (cleaning, offline)

- NO-SCHEDULE mode: Outside production calendar (offline)

- ENGINEERING mode: Engineering/testing activities outside production (stopped, offline)

State Transition Rules:

- Blocked/Starved/E-Stopped → Always classified as DOWNTIME (disabled mode)

- Production mode → Only allows actively producing states

- Minor stops (setup/changeover) → Counted within planned production time

- Scheduled maintenance → Excluded from OEE calculations

- Unscheduled workcenters → Automatically transition to no-schedule mode

Duration Calculation:

- Closes open records with precise ISO 8601 duration (PT#H#M#S)

- Calculates durationMinutes as decimal (rounded to 3 places)

- Uses occurAt and endAt timestamps for accurate period tracking

Batch Processing:

Generates three separate batch arrays for sequential execution:

1. Close Batches - Updates existing open records with endAt/duration

2. Create Batches - Inserts new history records with current state

3. Update Batches - Updates workcenter current state fields

Output Structure:

Returns array of batch objects, each containing:

- batchType: 'close', 'create', or 'update'

- batchIndex: Sequential batch number

- historyToClose/historyToCreate/workcentersToUpdate: Mutation payloads

- stats: Execution metadata (timezone, timestamp, record counts)

Execution Order:

Close → Create → Update ensures data integrity and prevents orphaned open records.

Error Handling:

- Validates required modes (no-schedule) and states (offline) exist

- Falls back to first available mode/state if required values missing

- Logs warnings when fallbacks are used

- Returns null if no batches generated (no state changes needed)

Configuration Parameters:

- batchSize: Number of workcenters per batch (default: 10)

- changeProb: Probability of state change per execution (default: 0.30)

- minProductionRatio: Minimum fraction in production mode (default: 0.40)

Schedule Integration:

- Uses currentScheduleByGroup mapping from upstream JSONata transform

- Applies scheduleId from active schedule for the workcenter's schedule group

- Transitions unscheduled workcenters to no-schedule mode automatically

This engine forms the core of the manufacturing simulation system, generating realistic operational data for OEE analysis, downtime tracking, and production monitoring dashboards.

header.name: Production Log
header.description:
**Production Log History**

This screen provides a centralized view of all production log entries, helping you track and analyze manufacturing activity over time. It is designed for operators, supervisors, and managers to monitor production performance and quality.

**Key Capabilities:**

- \*\*View Historical Records:\*\* Displays detailed logs of production runs, including timestamps, workcenter, work order, product, operator, and source.

- \*\*Performance Metrics:\*\* Shows quantities of good and scrap parts, total production, yield percentage, and cycle time for each entry.

- \*\*Filtering & Search:\*\* Use the filter panel to narrow results by date range, workcenter, work order, product, operator, schedule, or data source. Advanced GraphQL filtering is available for complex queries.

- \*\*Data Analysis Tools:\*\* Supports grouping, charting, and sorting to identify trends and improve decision-making.

- \*\*Actions:\*\* Quickly create new production entries, edit existing records, or delete logs. You can also refresh data and view detailed information for any record.

- \*\*Traceability:\*\* Each entry includes metadata such as who created it and when, ensuring full auditability.

This screen is essential for maintaining accurate production history, monitoring quality, and supporting continuous improvement initiatives.

header.name: Workcenter History
header.description:
**Workcenter History**

This screen provides a detailed timeline of operational states, modes, and events for each workcenter, enabling visibility into equipment behavior and downtime analysis.

**Purpose:**

- Track every state change (e.g., Production, Idle, Disabled) and associated events (e.g., Maintenance, Setup, Faults).

- Support OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) analysis by capturing availability and performance losses.

- Provide audit trails for compliance and continuous improvement.

**Key Features:**

- \*\*Historical Records:\*\* Displays start and end times, duration, workcenter, mode, state, event, work order, and schedule.

- \*\*Color-Coded Status:\*\* Modes and states use ISA-101 color standards for quick visual interpretation.

- \*\*Filtering & Search:\*\* Narrow results by date range, workcenter, work order, schedule, or mode. Advanced GraphQL filtering available for complex queries.

- \*\*Data Analysis Tools:\*\* Group, sort, and chart records to identify trends and root causes.

- \*\*Actions:\*\* Create new entries, edit existing records, delete, or refresh data. Each record includes notes and user attribution for traceability.

- \*\*Integration:\*\* Records can be created automatically via equipment signals or manually by operators.

This screen is essential for downtime tracking, shift performance comparison, and operational efficiency improvements.

props.description:
Workcenter History tracks all operational state changes, modes, and events for workcenters over time. Each record represents a discrete time period when a workcenter was in a specific operational state.

**Key Use Cases:**
• OEE Availability Analysis - Track production vs downtime
• Downtime Pareto Analysis - Identify top loss reasons
• State Timeline Visualization - See equipment behavior over time
• Shift Performance Comparison - Compare across schedules

**Data Flow:**
Records are created automatically by equipment integrations or manually by operators. Duration is calculated from occurAt and endAt timestamps. Events and categories enable drill-down analysis.

props.label: Code
props.description:
**`code`** (`String!`)
Unique identifier for this workcenter history record.

- Auto-generated or manually assigned.
- Format: `WCH-{SITE}-{SEQ}` (e.g., `WCH-DET-00001`).
- Used for audit trails and record lookups.

props.label: Occur At
props.description:
**`occurAt`** (`DateTime!`)
Timestamp when this operational state or event began.

- Critical for duration calculations and timeline analysis.
- Used in OEE availability calculations.
- Timezone-aware display based on user settings.

props.label: End At
props.description:
**`endAt`** (`DateTime`)
Timestamp when this operational state or event ended.

- Null if state is still active/ongoing.
- Used with occurAt to calculate duration.
- Essential for closed-loop state tracking.

props.label: Workcenter
props.description:
**`workcenter.code`** (`String!`)
The workcenter where this state/event occurred.

- Links to Workcenter master data.
- Required field - every history record must have a workcenter.
- Example: `WC-PRESS-01`, `WC-FILL-A`.

props.label: Mode
props.description:
**`modeId`** (`String`)
Operational mode of the workcenter during this period.

**ISA-101 Color Coding:**
• 🟢 **Production** (Green #2e7d32) - Active manufacturing
• 🟡 **Idle** (Amber #ed6c02) - Standby, available
• 🔴 **Disabled** (Red #d32f2f) - Unavailable, down

Mode determines OEE Availability calculation.

props.label: State
props.description:
**`stateId`** (`String`)
Detailed operational state within the current mode.

**ISA-101 Color Coding:**
• 🟢 **running** (Green) - Normal production
• 🟠 **running-slow** (Orange) - Producing with performance loss
• 🟠 **blocked** (Orange) - Downstream constraint
• 🟠 **starved** (Orange) - Upstream constraint
• 🟡 **stopped** (Amber) - Not producing, no fault
• 🟡 **held** (Amber) - Production hold
• 🔴 **faulted** (Red) - Equipment fault
• 🔴 **e-stopped** (Red) - Emergency stop
• 🔵 **changeover** (Blue) - Product changeover
• 🔵 **warmup** (Blue) - Equipment warming up
• 🔵 **cleaning** (Blue) - Cleaning cycle
• 🟣 **maintenance** (Purple) - Under maintenance
• ⚫ **offline/unknown** (Gray) - Unavailable or unknown

States drive OEE Performance and Availability analysis.

props.label: Event
props.description:
**`event.name`** (`String`)
Specific event or reason code for this state.

- Links to Event master data.
- Examples: `Scheduled Maintenance`, `Tool Change`, `Material Shortage`.
- Required for downtime analysis and Pareto charts.
- Displays 'No Event' when not applicable.

props.label: Event Category
props.description:
**`event.eventCategory.name`** (`String`)
High-level classification of the event.

- Groups events for reporting (e.g., Planned vs Unplanned).
- Examples: `Planned Downtime`, `Unplanned Downtime`, `Setup`, `Changeover`.
- Affects OEE calculations based on `affectsOee` flag.
- Displays 'Uncategorized' when not set.

props.label: Duration
props.description:
**`duration`** (`Duration`)
Calculated duration of this state period.

- Computed from occurAt and endAt timestamps.
- Displayed in abbreviated format (e.g., `45m`, `2h 30m`).
- Used for downtime totals and OEE calculations.
- Null/N/A if state is still active.

props.label: Schedule
props.description:
**`schedule.code`** (`String`)
Production schedule or shift during this period.

- Links to Schedule master data.
- Examples: `First`, `Second`, `Third`, `Weekend`.
- Enables shift-level performance analysis.
- Displays 'No Schedule' when not assigned.

props.label: Notes
props.description:
**`notes`** (`String`)
Free-text comments or observations.

- Operator-entered context about the state/event.
- May include root cause notes, actions taken, or follow-up items.
- Searchable for incident investigation.

props.label: Created At
props.description:
**`createdAt`** (`DateTime!`)
System timestamp when this record was created.

- Auto-populated by the system.
- Used for audit trails and data integrity.
- Cannot be modified after creation.

props.label: Created By
props.description:
**`createdByUser`** (`User!`)
User who created this record.

- Auto-populated based on logged-in user.
- Displays full name (First Last).
- Used for accountability and audit trails.

props.description: planned downtime in milliseconds for aggregation

props.description: unplanned downtime in milliseconds for aggregation

props.description: runtime in milliseconds for aggregation

header.name: Workcenter
header.description:
The Workcenter screen provides centralized management of manufacturing work centers within the industrial operations hierarchy. Work centers represent discrete production stations where manufacturing operations are performed, serving as the primary link between physical assets, production lines, and manufacturing cells.

**Key Features:**

- **Hierarchical Location Mapping**: Associates work centers with production lines and manufacturing cells for organizational clarity
- **ISA-101 State Management**: Tracks operational modes (Production, Idle, Disabled) and states (Running, Stopped, Held, Blocked, Starved, Faulted) following ISA-101 HMI standards
- **Work Order Integration**: Displays current work order assignments for active production tracking
- **Real-time Status Visibility**: Color-coded mode and state indicators provide at-a-glance operational status

**Filter Capabilities:**

- Workcenter code (partial match)
- Cell assignment
- Line assignment
- Operational mode
- Active/Inactive status
- Advanced GraphQL filtering

**CRUD Operations:**

- Create new work centers with cell/line assignments
- View detailed work center configuration
- Edit work center properties and assignments
- Duplicate existing work centers
- Deactivate work centers (soft delete)
- Delete work centers (with referential integrity protection)

**Data Model**: `Workcenter` **Module**: Machine Data Application **Group**: Machine Telemetry Site Application

startValue.title: Start Value
startValue.description: The starting value for the trendline. Say, if you want to plot a slanted trendline from value 102 to 109, the `startValue` will be 102.

displayValue.title: Display Value
displayValue.description: If you want to display a string caption for the trend line by its side, you can use this attribute. Example: `displayValue='Last Month High'`. When you don't supply this attribute, it automatically takes the value of `startValue`.

valueOnRight.title: Value On Right
valueOnRight.description: Whether to show the trend line value on left side or right side of chart. This is particularly useful when the trend line display values on the chart are colliding with divisional lines values on the chart.
